records.text: After John F. Kennedy was assassinated, the CIA allied with mainstream media and began trying to control people's minds.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: This is, to be clear, Operation Mockingbird on steroids, right? After JFK gets assassinated, the CIA gets into an alliance with the mainstream media and they begin trying to control our minds. Let's just repeat this.

verification.notes: Senate records confirm historical CIA relationships with journalists and concern that covert media operations could manipulate public opinion. However, documented CIA-media relationships and Project MOCKINGBIRD predated the November 1963 JFK assassination, and the claim that the alliance began afterward to control minds overstates and misdates the record.

sources.title: Church Committee Final Report, Book I
sources.relevance: Documents CIA relationships with journalists and concern about covert media manipulation; also shows the history did not begin after JFKs assassination.

records.text: Owens alleged that news media intentionally selected maroon-shirt photos of Tyler Robinson even though more recent photos showed him wearing other colors.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: I'm going to show you some photos that were presented in the media. If you Google Tyler Robinson in the media on that day, you will see these photos that they pulled from his mother's Facebook, even going back from when he was younger, photos of him and like, oh gosh, wow, this kid must just love maroon shirts. ... It's his favorite shirt. short. That was intentional. ... That was intentional because I actually had gone through his mother's Facebook at the time, and there were plenty of other photos of Tyler Robinson to choose from, many of them much more recent than the one that they were showing of him wearing shirts of all different color varieties, blue shirts, white shirts, green shirts.

verification.notes: Reviewed the accusation in transcript context and reopened AFP's original-image investigation. AFP confirms that an authentic maroon-shirt family photograph circulated and was published by news outlets; it does not establish coordinated editorial intent to condition identification of a decoy. The core accusation is therefore unresolved, not partly verified merely because the photograph exists. No newsroom direction, coordination record, or comparative publication dataset was located.

sources.relevance: Confirms the original photograph's maroon shirt and publication history, not a coordinated identification operation.
